result.rationale: The Healthy band is correctly computed and well-supported: 5 DPD on the worst line and no adverse news produce 4.3, far below the 35 Watch threshold, and the €114,399 owed across 3 open invoices sits within the €210,000 CL05 credit line. However, the score keys off a point-in-time DPD and therefore cannot reflect the deteriorating pattern the payment review documents (settled invoices at 0 → 4 → 9 days late, with the oldest open invoice now 5 days past due). That trajectory is not sufficient to move the band — the gap to Watch is too wide — but it warrants active monitoring, particularly as a further ~€80k falls due in the coming weeks. Note also that the 0.0 news score reflects no matched articles rather than a confirmed clean record, though at 0.35 weight even a maximum-severity hit would leave this buyer in Healthy.

concerns.issue: Score uses worst DPD of 5 as a point-in-time input and does not capture the deteriorating trend flagged in the payment review: settled invoices went from on-time to 4 days late to 9 days late. A 5-DPD snapshot understates a buyer whose lateness is widening each cycle; recommend re-scoring on the next settlement rather than waiting for a scheduled cycle.
Trend confidence is limited by thin history — only 3 settled invoices underpin the deteriorating assessment, which the payment agent itself rates as moderate confidence.

Exposure is concentrated with a single insurer (CL05) holding the only credit line; there is no diversification of credit exposure across insurers, and the payment review advises against any limit increase pending further evidence.
Two further invoices totaling ~€80k fall due in the coming weeks. Given the widening days-late pattern, these are the key test of whether the Healthy band remains appropriate.
